title: Localizing the Tag Comparisons in the Wakeup Logic to Reduce Energy Consumption of the Issue Queue
problem: The issue queue's wakeup logic performs global tag comparisons across all entries, consuming significant energy. This global comparison overhead represents a critical bottleneck in processor power consumption.
motivation: The issue queue is one of the largest energy consumers in microprocessors, making energy reduction in the wakeup logic critical for efficient processor design.
method: SegWU segments the wakeup logic logically based on partial tag bits. Instructions dispatch to segment entries using partial bits of source tags, and at wakeup time, destination tags compare only within the matching segment, eliminating unnecessary comparisons in other segments.
key_novelty: Segmenting the wakeup logic based on partial tag bits to localize tag comparisons, eliminating unnecessary comparisons across the entire issue queue.
contributions: Proposed SegWU architecture that segments wakeup logic based on partial tag bit matching
Achieved 90.3% reduction in tag comparison operations
3.0% net reduction in core energy consumption excluding secondary effects
6.9% overall energy reduction including secondary effects with zero performance degradation

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 3.0% net core energy reduction; 6.9% overall with secondary effects

primary_theme: Energy-efficient issue queue via localized tag comparisons
